A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReplaceMe, with matching authors, core methodology, and primary experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and the complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM and CLIP pruning experiments, calibration and optimization ablations, model-scaling results, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original pruning experiments and adds benchmark evaluations, healing experiments, and results varying the number of linear transformations.

M1.justification: The block-selection procedure, LS/cosine objectives, transformation fusion, and multiple-transform framework remain. v3 specifies and evaluates an optional post-pruning procedure that fine-tunes only the linear transformation while freezing the remaining model weights (A.14–A.15); v1 discusses healing without this specific procedure.

E1.justification: A.13 adds BBH, MATH, GPQA, MuSR, and MMLU-Pro evaluations, substantially extending coverage of complex reasoning, competition mathematics, and expert knowledge. A.14 also introduces C4 data for healing. The earlier language, vision, and calibration datasets remain represented.

E2.justification: The external pruning comparator sets in the principal LLM and CLIP comparisons remain unchanged. The new healing study explicitly evaluates full-model fine-tuning as a comparator for LT-only healing (Table 12). The added harder-benchmark evaluation reuses UIDL.

E3.justification: v3 introduces controlled healing comparisons with different trainable weights, learning rates, GPU counts, and step budgets (Tables 12 and 14). A.16 fixes eight pruned layers and varies 1, 2, 4, or 8 transformations on Llama and Mistral. A.1 also changes the stated compression-ratio calculation from layer counts to parameter counts; this does not establish reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: New analyses test LT-only versus full-model healing, quantify healed ReplaceMe's computational costs, and systematically examine sensitivity to transformation count (A.8, A.14, A.16). These substantially extend evidence about recovery mechanisms and tradeoffs. Calibration-size and masking analyses are retained through relocation to A.12.

E5.justification: A.5 retains the same unspecified multiple-run reporting: accuracy mean 60.71 with standard deviation 0.08, and Lambada perplexity mean 15.90 with standard deviation 0.05. No run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical tests are added.

E6.justification: v3 adds benchmark profiles in Figure 7, healing and efficiency results, and detailed LT-count results. Table 12 newly reports average accuracies of 0.61295 without healing, 0.64432 with LT-only healing, and 0.64657 with full-model healing. Most primary scores remain unchanged. v1's Multi_LT (Cosine) result with perplexity 19.06 disappears; the LS result 18.99 is retained as 18.9853 in Table 15.

T1.justification: A.1 changes the quantities in the formal compression-ratio definition from numbers of layers to numbers of parameters, resolving an inconsistency with its parameter-reduction description. The least-squares derivation and constrained-transformation solutions are retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v3 removes the conclusion's claim that ReplaceMe is the first training-free depth-pruning method. The main contributions and headline claim of approximately 90% performance retention at up to 25% pruning remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning mathematical-task sensitivity, the tradeoff in transformation count, and the usefulness of LT-only healing. Its Limitations section makes model-size and architecture dependence explicit, although the need for healing at high compression was already stated. A.13 calls the MATH degradation marginal despite the substantially larger drop plotted in Figure 7.

D1.justification: v3 substantially improves implementation disclosure: Adam learning rate 0.0001, batch size 1024, ten epochs, identity initialization, and no bias; hardware and software specifications; and detailed healing configurations (A.15, Tables 13–14). These details do not establish changes to the retained calibration experiments. The repository was already linked in v1.

R1.justification: Related Work adds discussion of Your Transformer Is Secretly Linear and its earlier block-linearization approach. v3 also adds benchmark and evaluation-framework references and removes the ExpandNets citation and associated overparameterization statement. The broader positioning among pruning approaches remains.

P1.justification: v3 renames the title and some subsections, polishes existing prose, moves calibration-size and masking discussion into A.12, and inserts a dedicated Limitations section. The overall narrative and organization of the core method and experiments remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 3 changes from one combined plot to three model-specific panels. The computational-efficiency triptych becomes a logarithmic normalized bar chart, and v3 adds radar plots plus healing, configuration, and LT-count tables. Calibration displays move to the appendix and multiple-transform tables are reorganized. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens reproducibility through concrete implementation details and adds useful evidence about harder tasks, healing, and transformation count. Its narrower novelty claim and added prior-work discussion improve positioning. However, the new benchmark evaluation lacks detailed settings, and its substantial MATH degradation is understated in the prose, limiting the overall gain.
